main_integration_review.scope: Main independently checked vocabulary/page locations, chapter boundaries, source emphasis spot-checks and cue scope/reuse. Original author-pending statements below are chronological draft notes superseded by this review. No clinical, human expert, recall or render validation.
main_integration_review.normalizations: Line-wrap hyphens, beta and punctuation normalized. Chapter23 wet surface expands wet or conducting surface; Chapter25 calcium gluconate expands Calcium chloride or gluconate; blood volume also appears as blood and plasma volume. Shared-word expansions are not contiguous quotations.
main_integration_review.family_collision_warning: Qualify co-occurring family cues such as atrial/ventricular fibrillation, calcium salts or gangrene subtypes; family reuse is not exact subtype discrimination.

entries.cue: Recognizably pregnant study mannequin with a rounded abdomen.
entries.reason: Newly recorded familiar category in the bounded banks/catalog/workshops checked, not a new human-model primitive. Appearance is a mnemonic convention, not proof of pregnancy, gestational age, body-size criterion or a claim about every pregnant person's appearance.

entries.cue: Recognizable camera aperture diaphragm shown as overlapping iris blades.
entries.reason: Newly recorded double meaning, not a novel camera ingredient. Learner must know the camera part's name; it may otherwise be called shutter or aperture. No analogy about breathing mechanics or anatomical equivalence is asserted.

entries.cue: Simple study torso with a conspicuous belly button.
entries.cue_scope: Familiar belly-button synonym for the learned headword
entries.reason: New literal target record, not revival or resolution of the rejected naval-ship/navel sound attempt. Belly button supplies a familiar anatomical synonym; not a procedural landmark, gestational measure or instruction involving the abdomen.

entries.cue: Study mannequin lying flat on its back, face upward.
entries.reason: Newly recorded simple position token; no added equipment or sound fragments. Not a recommendation for any patient, a resuscitation setup or a statement about positional effects.

entries.cue: A toy torso with an unmistakable left hand tilts toward its own left side on a plain tabletop.
entries.cue_scope: Left plus side plus tilt vocabulary
entries.reason: New familiar directional relationship, not a copied source figure or a positioning demonstration. Viewer-left versus subject-left remains a recognition risk; no angle, wedge placement, clinical use or benefit is encoded.

entries.cue: Nearly empty transparent reservoir connected in a closed circulation loop, with red liquid low at its bottom.
entries.reason: Same Chapter7/13 family. No cause, volume criterion, pregnancy effect or fluid recommendation imported.

entries.cue: Tube visibly inside a transparent freestanding windpipe model.
entries.cue_scope: Existing intubation family token within an identified airway context
entries.reason: Reuse at the broader selected headword, not a new cue or an assertion that all intubation is endotracheal. No insertion route, depth, confirmation, technique or patient-specific recommendation.

entries.cue: Transparent pipe visibly leaking red liquid into a puddle.
entries.reason: Same red-fluid leak, without a control clamp. No site, amount, cause, obstetric association or intervention inferred from the table.

entries.cue: Plug lodged inside a vessel visibly running through a lung model, not an airway.
entries.reason: Reuses established learned category without adding material or origin qualifiers. Not a diagnostic illustration, pregnancy-risk statement or clinical mechanism lesson.

entries.cue_scope: Magnesium/magnet plus sulfur/rotten-eggs partial learned name reminder
entries.reason: Exact Chapter19 composition with two existing user primitives, not a new combination. Sulfate ending is not fully encoded. No claim about magnetism, smell, chemical equivalence or a medication use; source table's other columns excluded.

entries.cue: A familiar freestanding table lamp with a conspicuous lampshade.
entries.cue_scope: Lamp/lamp-s partial learned name reminder within an eclampsia lesson
entries.reason: Newly recorded partial-name object, not exact full-name phonetics. Lamp alone does not encode the opening or ending, distinguish preeclampsia, or identify a diagnosis without lesson context. No clinical sign, mechanism or management implied; recall untested.

entries.cue: A transparent reservoir containing red liquid, shown without a high or low modifier.
entries.reason: New neutral headword record reuses reservoir/red-fluid ingredients without the low-state modifier of hypovolemia. No bodily distribution or amount asserted. Untested vocabulary association only; no clinical relationships, mechanisms, thresholds or instructions encoded.
